metadata.name: Ecodesign for Ruby / Rails
metadata.description: Ecodesign rules for Ruby and Rails code: sober ActiveRecord, batched traversal, lazy enumerators, expiring caches.

donnees.name: Ruby — data access (ActiveRecord)
donnees.description: Load only the columns and rows actually used (RGESN Backend, GR491_Backend_2/3).

rules.title: Whole table walked in memory
rules.description: .all.each and .all.map instantiate one ActiveRecord object per row: memory and CPU proportional to the table size.
rules.recommendation: find_each/in_batches for large volumes; paginate every exposed list (pagy, kaminari).

rules.title: Full objects loaded for a single column
rules.description: map(&:col) instantiates every object when only one column is read.
rules.recommendation: pluck(:col) or select(:col1, :col2); includes/preload/eager_load on the associations you walk, to avoid the N+1.

rules.title: Counting where an existence test is enough
rules.description: count > 0, or any? on a relation, runs a full count when the database could stop at the first row.
rules.recommendation: exists? for an existence test; update_all/insert_all for bulk writes, never save inside a loop.

memoire.name: Ruby — memory and CPU
memoire.description: Avoid intermediate arrays and linear searches (RGESN Algorithms).

rules.title: Linear search on a large array
rules.description: include? walks the whole array; repeated in a loop, the processing turns quadratic.
rules.recommendation: Index into a Set or a Hash before the loop.

rules.title: String concatenation in a loop
rules.description: `s += ...` allocates a new string on every iteration, where mutation reuses the buffer.
rules.recommendation: Build with << (mutation); lazy enumerators (.lazy) and each_slice for long transformation chains.

taches.name: Ruby — cache, jobs and I/O
taches.description: Bound caches, do not poll, reuse connections (RGESN Backend/Hosting).

rules.title: Cache entry with no expiry
rules.description: A Rails.cache.fetch or write without expires_in holds the entry indefinitely, including once the data is no longer read.
rules.recommendation: Always pass expires_in; never a constant or class variable that accumulates without limit.

rules.title: High-frequency scheduled job
rules.description: A periodic job watching a state consumes CPU and database capacity continuously to catch a rare change.
rules.recommendation: Idempotent, batched jobs; event-driven triggering rather than polling; outbound HTTP connections and the database pool reused.
